1B.why: I drew a cheerful lantern fish to give our unfolding story a curious guide carrying its own light.

1A.why: A night moth with glowing eyespots opens the story under an empty sky, inviting others to add the lamp, the garden, or the darkness it flies through.

1C.why: I drew a lighthouse riding a gentle sky whale to guide lost travelers into our shared story.

1D.why: A lit lantern hung in the middle of an empty canvas: a first light for the others to gather around and build the story out from.

2B.why: I grew a luminous smiling moonflower beneath the surviving moth so its midnight flight has a welcoming destination.

2A.why: The moth needed a light to circle, so a warm candle lantern now hangs beneath it, its glow spilling into the dark and giving the story a heart.

2C.why: I planted a luminous moonflower beneath the winning moth so its midnight journey has nectar and a welcoming glow.

2D.why: A hooded wanderer raises a lantern beneath the moth, giving the great moth a light to be drawn to and the story a traveller.

3D.why: A hooded wanderer comes in from the dark on the left, lantern held out toward the glowing bloom, so the story now has someone walking toward the light the moth found.

3C.why: I drew a smiling frog wizard tending the moonflower with a star-tipped wand, giving the moth garden a kindly caretaker.

3B.why: I drew a spiral-shelled snail carrying a sealed letter toward the moonflower, turning our luminous garden into the beginning of a delivery adventure.

3A.why: The bloom needed roots, so it now grows from a terracotta pot on a windowsill, with a snail and a ladybug keeping the moth company on the night watch.

4A.why: The night needed a sky, so a crescent moon rises over the garden with a small cat perched in its curve, watching the moth circle the bloom below.

4B.why: I gave the winning snail a heart-marked woodland mailbox beyond the moonflower so its patient delivery ends with a welcoming home.

4D.why: A cottage with lit windows and a crescent moon on the empty right edge, so the moth, the glowing bloom and the beehive become the night garden of someone's home.

4C.why: I added a fox gardener pouring silver water toward the moonflower, completing a small world where every creature helps the garden thrive.

why.A: The lantern is crisp, readable and answers the moth directly, the figure on the whale is charming but busier, and the fish with sparkles is hardest to read at a glance.
why.B: The lighthouse whale tells the most inventive story, the moth has beautifully patterned wings, and the lantern provides a strong warm focal point.
why.C: The moth has the richest wing patterns and strongest silhouette, the lantern creates a clear story focal point, and the charming fish is partly obscured.
why.D: The moth is crisp, symmetric and instantly readable; the red-hatted figure on the boat is charming but busier; the blue creature is hard to make out.

why.A: The glowing bloom is a full, coherent picture that adds a garden to the night, the vine is a nice thread but mostly hidden, and the remaining fragments of B do not form a readable image.
why.B: The white moonflower remains the clearest and most graceful addition beneath the moth, followed by the surviving green structure and then the mostly obscured sparkles.
why.C: Among the surviving pixels, B keeps delicate pink petals and lively foliage, D retains an intriguing grounded silhouette, and A is reduced mostly to scattered sparks.
why.D: The glowing white-and-cyan bloom under the moth is complete and reads as the moth's flower; B shows only hands and vines but still adds to the scene, while A is almost entirely covered.

why.A: The hooded lamp-bearer is crisp and adds a character to the night, the beehive is a solid readable shape that extends the garden, and the purple bud plant is pleasant but its stems and leaves blur together.
why.B: The lantern-bearing traveler adds the strongest story character, the terracotta pot elegantly grounds the surviving flower, and the partly covered green figure is harder to read.
why.C: The spiral-shelled snail adds the most expressive new character, the terracotta pot beautifully grounds the moonflower, and the lantern keeper supplies a warm but simpler silhouette.
why.D: The beehive is crisp, complete and belongs in this night garden; the wooden chest is clean but a stranger to the scene; the green sprite is fragmented and hard to read where it overlaps.

why.A: The little house on its post is the crispest and most complete picture, the orange bird is charming but its outline gets busy, and the seated figure is too broken up by overlaps to read clearly.
why.B: The cat nestled in the crescent moon has the strongest complete silhouette and storybook atmosphere, followed by the expressive fox and then the more obscured cottage.
why.C: The cat perched on a crescent moon gives the story a beautiful ending, the heart-marked mailbox adds delightful character, and the cottage is harder to read after overlap.
why.D: The cat curled on the crescent moon is clean, complete and the perfect closing image for a night garden; the red house is whole but heavy; the orange fox is buried under it and only its head remains.
